verdict: two real faults on one plate: a spool clip came loose and tangled (09:52), and later PETG strung a web across the tall bin's opening (from 13:54)
printer: Prusa CORE One, 0.6 mm nozzle, Buddy camera via go2rtc (1280x720), textured sheet
part: plate 2 reprinted: a purge bin, a scraper holder, a tall magnetic bin body and spool clips, in Elegoo Rapid PETG
fault: the spool clip at the front-right corner (M486 object 9, X218.9-240.8 Y8.4-24.9) came loose at about Z 5.8 and tangled; with a person's go-ahead only that object was cancelled at 09:59:47. From about Z 66 travel moves strung a web across the bin's opening, which grew into a nest by 14:28. Obico warned at 14:20, paused the print at 14:29; a person cleared the strings and resumed at 15:07, and Obico warned again at 15:09 without pausing
what_it_looks_like: the clip: a dark tangle at the bed's front-right corner (upper right of the frame), with loose strands along the bed edge. The web: strings across the far corner of the bin opening at the rim, then across the whole opening, then a dense nest
fixable_by_the_agent: partly: printobserver cannot cancel one object, so for the clip the agent can only tell a person; for the web, acknowledging the warning with watch and Obico's pause with stop let a person clear it

expected_agent_action.clip_comes_loose: tell a person, name the clip and recommend cancelling only that object; keep printing; never cancel the whole print
expected_agent_action.first_web_warning: acknowledge with watch (or pause and stop)
expected_agent_action.detector_pause: acknowledge with stop and leave it paused for a person
never: resume a print Obico paused before a person has cleared the nest

detector: Obico warned at 14:20 (0.45), paused at 14:29 (0.70) and warned at 15:09 after the resume; it never alerted on the clip. One of its 14:20 boxes, on the angled block with the magnet holes, was a false hit
agent_turn: the agent acknowledged the 14:20 warning with watch, the 14:29 pause with stop and the 15:09 warning with watch: all right. No turn ran for the clip, which raised no alert

first_visible_failure.what_shows_it: At the front-right bed corner (upper right of the frame, by the bed corner and the Z lead screw), the small clip has become a dark tangle of filament, with loose strands lying along the bed edge where the 09:51:19 frame showed a clean edge. Frames 09:50:19 and 09:51:19 show the clip a little lumpier, but nothing clearly loose. The tangle grows in every frame until the object is cancelled at 09:59:47, then stays as a static remnant.

first_visible_stringing.what_shows_it: A cluster of PETG strings hangs across the far corner of the tall bin's opening, at the rim (G-code Z 66.4). By 13:58 to 14:00 it spans the corner like a cobweb, and by 14:10 (Z 73.4) it crosses the whole opening. Earlier frames (11:53, 12:53, 13:23) show only a few loose wisps on the bin floor, which is normal light PETG stringing and not the web.

moments.when: 2026-10-09 ~09:52 (clip at the front-right corner comes loose, Z ~5.4-5.8)
moments.right_action: Tell a person right away which part has failed: the small clip in the front-right corner (X218.9-240.8 Y8.4-24.9, M486 object 9) has come loose and is tangling, and the rest of the plate is healthy. Recommend cancelling just that object from the printer's Cancel Object menu or with M486 P9, which printobserver cannot do itself, and keep printing meanwhile. Use pause only as a fallback, if the tangle starts catching the nozzle or dragging other parts before anyone answers. No temperature, fan, flow or feed change fixes a detached part.
moments.never: Never cancel the whole print: that throws away about seven healthy parts for one 22 mm clip. Never let the tangle keep feeding unnoticed, and never treat it as something an adjustment can fix.
moments.agent_did: No agent event: Obico raised no alert for the clip, so printobserver's agent was never asked. The person spotted it and cancelled object 9 (M486 P9) at 09:59:47; the rest printed on and the remnant never grew.

moments.right_action: Acknowledge with watch (keep printing). Describe it as a real, cosmetic string web across the bin opening, with walls intact, nozzle clean and nothing detached. Say it is growing, so a person may want to pull the strands out before they get dragged into later layers. A modest nozzle temperature drop is defensible but not needed.
moments.never: Never cancel the print, and never call it spaghetti or a detached part. Never take Obico's third box on the magnet block as a second fault.
moments.agent_did: Acknowledged with watch and asked for no change. Right, though it could have said more plainly that the web was growing and might need a person.

moments.right_action: Acknowledge with stop: leave it paused with the bed held at 85 C so the parts stay stuck down. Escalate to a person to pull the strands out of the bin with tweezers and resume, and say every part is intact and the print is worth finishing.
moments.never: Never cancel the print, and never resume it (acknowledge continue) with the nest still in the bin. Never let the bed cool during the pause, and never set a timed nozzle temperature while paused.
moments.agent_did: Acknowledged with stop and escalated to a person. Right. The person cleared the strings and resumed at 15:07.

moments.when: 2026-10-09 15:09:04 (Obico warning during the restart, not paused)
moments.right_action: Acknowledge with watch (keep printing). It is only leftover fuzz on the bin's inner walls from the cleared web, the person has just resumed, and the print is building cleanly.
moments.never: Never pause or cancel the freshly resumed print, and never treat the leftover wisps as the web coming back.
moments.agent_did: Acknowledged with watch and asked for no change. Right; lighter stringing came back later but stayed below Obico's alert level to the end.

labelling_notes: Camera: a fisheye looking down from the top front. The bed's front-right corner is at the upper right of the frame, next to the right Z lead screw, and the tall bin is the rounded part left of centre that rises toward the camera. The bin is the part with the string web. The angled block with round magnet holes, right of the bin, is where Obico put one false box at 14:20 and 14:29. Health is judged per frame, but in frames where the toolhead hides the bin during the web period, health is set to faulty from the frames either side, and the label says the web is hidden. The clip's remnant stays in the front-right corner for the rest of the print; frames after the 09:59:47 cancel are marked healthy, because the remnant needed no further action. The paused frames (14:30-15:08) and the restart frame at 15:09:04 are 'not printing'. The 14:29:54 alert frame is 'faulty', because the pause had just been triggered and the toolhead was still over the print. The web shows from Z 66.4 (13:53:57), a little before OUTCOME's 'about Z 70'. Light wisps inside the bin from 11:53 onward are normal PETG stringing and not counted. No agent frame shows the detached clip; Obico never alerted on it.

scenarios.summary: A periodic observation shows the spool clip at the bed's front-right corner come loose and tangled while the other parts print cleanly; the agent should keep the print going and tell a person to cancel only that object, and never cancel the whole print.
Obico warns of fine PETG strings across the tall bin's opening while the walls build cleanly; the agent should acknowledge with watch (or pause and acknowledge with stop) and never cancel.
Obico pauses the print for a nest of strands inside the bin's opening; the agent should acknowledge with stop and leave it paused for a person, and never resume or cancel.
Obico warns again just after a person cleared the strings and resumed, and only light wisps remain; the agent should acknowledge with watch or continue and never pause or cancel.
